lacuna.name: moe-kernels-sm75
lacuna.repo_anchor: The gap is recorded at three house anchors. (1) plan/0002-turing-marlin-backend/marlin-contract.md section '## MoE (completed)' (the contract study, not the integration): "`marlin_moe.py` exposes `fused_marlin_moe` and `batched_fused_marlin_moe`, both funneling into `_fused_marlin_moe` and the `marlin_moe_gemm` custom op over `MarlinExpertsBase` ... Semantics: expert weights in the same Marlin packed format (`w13`/`w2`, num_bits 4 or 8), grouped/batched GEMM over the routed expert list, top-k weights applied outside the kernel. A Turing MoE path reuses the dense Turing GEMM behind the same expert interface; no separate MoE kernel architecture is planned." (2) The still-open stage in plan/0002 README, '### Integrate Marlin MoE {#moe-integration}' (depends: #dense-integration): "Adapt the validated Turing GEMM machinery to the Marlin expert abstraction: preserve expert weight semantics and grouped/batched GEMM semantics ... and repeat numerical and performance validation with expert shapes added to the adversary"; MEMORY 2026-08-28 records the program state "Open: optimized kernel ..., MoE, runtime/graph validation, D8 report". (3) plan/0005-format-interop/README.md 'Operator target': "if the target checkpoint is the MoE variant, the MoE grouped forward is already oracle-validated (plan/0002)" - i.e. validated semantics, untuned kernel. The outline item moe-kernels-sm75 (category: ecosystem-strategy) is the lacuna statement itself.
lacuna.current_status: As of 2026-09-07 the upstream MoE-kernel stack crossed the Turing floor in three waves, and the operator-relevant checkpoints all exist. (1) Marlin-for-Turing: PR #29901 '[Kernel][Quantization][MoE] add marlin kernel support for turing (sm75)' (jinzhen-lin, merged 2025-12-16) covers dense AND MoE Marlin on sm75 for GPTQ/AWQ/FP8/NVFP4 weights with FP16 (and INT8 for GPTQ/AWQ) activations - Turing adaptations: synchronous global->shared copies (no cp.async), m16n8k8 stacked twice for k16, and a temporary FP16 accumulator because FP32-accumulate halves Turing MMA throughput; MXFP4 was explicitly excluded ('requires BF16 activation'; the author's MXFP4xFP16 variant reverted at mgoin's request), and a follow-up commenter (mokieli) reports a BF16-related failure running a Qwen3-Next AWQ model on Tesla T4s. PR #31000 (2025-12-19) lowered the compressed-tensors Marlin gates 8.0 -> 7.5; first release carrying the set is v0.14.0 (2026-01-16/20, torch 2.9.1, cu129). (2) Humming (the sub-4-bit MoE lane): vLLM humming.py get_min_capability() = 75, 'FP16 activations on SM75+ (Turing floor; BF16 needs SM80+)'; integration PRs #34556 (2026-04-24), #46389 'Humming support for 2/3/5/6/7-bit pack-quantized weight-only' (2026-06-24, first release v0.25.0), and #48918 '[CT] Support Humming for WNA16 MoE' (yiliu30, merged 2026-08-19) which 'allows the Humming path to initialize for sub-byte WNA16 checkpoints instead of hard-failing in the Marlin-only path' - validated on the mixed 2-bit-expert checkpoint INC4AI/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-Attn4bits-Mlp2bits-AutoRound (GSM8K 5-shot 0.909), follow-up bugfix #53163 (unset group_size normalization). #48918 is IN the fork's lane tip (commit 54dd98be28 under 711b6898c46c, 2026-09-07); humming-kernels[cu13]==0.1.12 is a standard requirement in requirements/cuda.txt. (3) Open crash surface, both closed not-planned/stale and unfixed: #35922 (2026-03-03) on A100 (SM80) with compressed-tensors Qwen3-30B-A3B - W4A16-INT4 MoE dies with 'CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered' in fused_marlin_moe, and ALL FP4 MoE modes (NVFP4A16/MXFP4A16/NVFP4 W4A4) die with 'CUDA error: no kernel image is available for execution on the device' (FP4 MoE kernels not compiled for SM80), while dense FP4 works and everything works on SM89/SM90; related #29361 (fused_marlin_moe illegal access, Kimi-K2 on H20) and #33416 (NVFP4 MoE missing SM120). #38022 (2026-03-24) - Marlin MoE MXFP4 gpt-oss-20b crashes even on Blackwell RTX PRO 6000 with 'Invalid thread config: thread_m_blocks = 4, thread_k = -1, thread_n = -1, num_threads = -1' at MKN=[32768, 2880, 2880]: the kernel requires K and N divisible by 128 and 2880 is only 32-aligned; workaround FP8 dynamic, --enforce-eager does not help; assertion source verified in the fork tree at csrc/libtorch_stable/moe/marlin_moe_wna16/ops.cu:500. (4) Model mix (the demand side): Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (config.json: 256 experts top-8, moe_intermediate 512, hidden 2048, 40 layers, hybrid 3:1 linear-attention:full-attention (GDN-class), shared_expert_intermediate 512, GQA 2 KV heads, head_dim 256, MTP-1, 262144 ctx, ViT tower, bfloat16); Intel/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-int2-mixed-CT-AutoRound (created 2026-07-23): routed MoE experts INT2 group 64, attention/linear-attention/shared-expert INT4 group 128, compressed-tensors WNA16 pack-quantized, ~14.47 GB stored, 'requires vLLM support for compressed-tensors WNA16 MoE checkpoints with the Humming backend' (PR #48918); accuracy caveat ON the card: 'The measured accuracy varies significantly across different backends' - quantized GSM8K 0.1585 (lmeval/vllm) vs 0.8370 (evalscope/vllm). gpt-oss-20b: 32 experts top-4, hidden_size=intermediate_size=2880 (the #38022 shape), MXFP4-native - on stock vLLM+T4 declared 'impossible' in a 2025-era forum thread (FA3/FlashInfer attention floor), MXFP4 needs CC>=9.0 for native paths and dequantizes via Triton elsewhere. Gemma 4 (2026-04-02, Apache-2.0): gemma-4-26B-A4B-it MoE, 26B total / 4B active, 128 fine-grained experts top-8, multimodal, Day-0 vLLM recipe (the outline's '27B-A4B' is a mislabel of 26B-A4B - correction). Qwen3.8-27B (dense, the sibling of this item's dense program) and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (2026-08-26, 125B-A6B, GDN + Qwen Sparse Attention) define the operator's model line. (5) Fused-MoE Triton tuning configs: the lane-tip tree ships 331 config JSONs under vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/configs/ and the device histogram is exclusively flagship - H100 (62), H200 (51), MI300X (34), B200 (33), A100 (32), H20 (19), MI325X (19), GB200, L40S (4), RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, RTX 4090 (2), GB10 (2) - with NO T4, 2080 Ti, or RTX 6000 (Turing) entry at any E/N; E=256 (the Qwen3.6-35B class) exists only for A100/MI325X/L40S and mostly fp8/int8 dtypes. get_moe_configs matches exact device names only, and on miss logs 'Using default MoE config. Performance might be sub-optimal! Config file not found at %s' (fused_moe.py:1168) - the documented escape hatches are VLLM_TUNED_CONFIG_FOLDER plus benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_moe.py tuning (a vLLM forum thread for exactly 'Config file not found Qwen3.6-35B-A3B' recommends the tuner), and community repo MissionSquad/vllm-moe-configs patches the tuner for single-GPU/older setups. (6) The Triton gate on the Triton-MoE path: Triton >= 3.3 emits NO tensor-core math for tl.dot below cc 8.0 (PR #5066, merged 2024-11-05; the April 2026 restore attempt #9970 was declined: 'We don't want to officially support Turing'), so the fused-MoE Triton kernel is FMA-bound on sm75 under modern pins; at tag v3.2.0 the mapping is source-verified: getMMAVersionSafe maps computeCapability 75-89 to MMAv2, with sm75 set to versionMinor=1 (v2.1) - i.e. a Triton 3.2 pin restores m16n8k8 tensor-core codegen for the fused-MoE dots (the GDN item's finding generalized), and stock vLLM v0.8.x is the natural carrier of that pin (torch 2.6.0 + triton 3.2.0 pairing).
lacuna.sm75_viability: What actually runs on Turing-class hardware today, per backend. (a) Marlin MoE WNA16 (GPTQ/AWQ INT4/INT8 symmetric, FP8, NVFP4A16): nominally sm75-open since #29901/#31000 (compressed_tensors wNa16 scheme get_min_capability = 75, code-verified in the fork tree; marlin_utils floors at capability 75), but public sm75 MoE validation is thin - the PR's quoted benchmarks are dense GEMMs, and the one post-merge T4 datapoint in its thread is a BF16/AWQ failure report [uncertain: whether upstream CI or anyone validated the MoE path on real sm75 silicon]. The house-measured sm75 yardsticks: incumbent dense Marlin 51-57 TFLOP/s at M512 (locked 1455 MHz), fork kernels opt1/opt2 23-25 TFLOP/s - the MoE path reuses exactly this machinery behind MarlinExpertsBase (per the plan/0002 contract), so dense perf acceptance is the MoE perf ceiling. Alignment floor: Marlin MoE thread-config requires K,N % 128 - gpt-oss-20b's 2880 shapes crash (#38022), Qwen3.6-35B-A3B's 512/2048/1024 (TP2) shapes are clean; a loud load-time gate is mandatory because upstream's is a runtime assert. (b) Humming WNA16 MoE (INT1-8 symmetric + dynamic zero point, FP16 activations, SM75+ floor, min capability 75 code-verified; humming-kernels 0.1.12 pinned): the only upstream sub-4-bit MoE route with a Turing floor and the designated backend for the Intel int2-mixed-CT checkpoint; W2A16 regression tests and a fused_moe oracle harness (fused_moe/oracle/int_wna16.py) exist in-tree; no public sm75 humming MoE run found [uncertain: real-device sm75 behavior of humming JIT dispatch and its accuracy vs the harness-divergent card numbers]. (c) Triton fused-MoE (the int4_w4a16/fp16/bf16 family): runs on sm75 but doubly penalized - zero tuned configs for any Turing device (exact device-name keying; default-config fallback warning) and FMA-only tl.dot codegen on Triton >= 3.3; under a Triton 3.2 pin the dots ride m16n8k8 (FP32-accumulate at half Turing MMA rate, per #29901's own note), and configs tuned under one codegen regime mis-select under the other - tuning and pinning must be settled together. (d) FP4 MoE: closed or crashing on/below this class - FP4 Marlin MoE kernels are not compiled below SM89 (#35922, cudaErrorNoKernelImageForDevice on SM80), Marlin MXFP4 is excluded on Turing (BF16-only, #29901), gpt-oss MXFP4 needs the fork's own recast/LUT emulation lane instead (mxfp4-nvfp4-ecosystem item). (e) Attention-backend matrix for these MoE models on sm75: stock vLLM declares gpt-oss unservable on T4 (FA3/FlashInfer floor); the fork's own sm75 attention port (plan/0002 flash_fwd_sm75.cuh line) plus FLA-Triton GDN (FMA-bound, separate item) is what makes the hybrid MoEs (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B is 3:1 linear:full) servable at all - the MoE item composes with both. Existence proofs: 67ailab guide (2026-03-21) runs Qwen3.5-35B-A3B GPTQ-Int4 (same 256-expert GDN-hybrid class) on 4x T4 TP=4 at ~4.4 GB weights/card with PROJECTED ~10-20 tok/s bs1 (estimates, no measured run); weicj/vLLM-2080Ti-Definitive serves Marlin FP8/INT4/NVFP4 on dual modded 2080 Ti with Qwen3.6-27B-FP8 (dense) as primary route. No measured Turing fused-MoE throughput numbers exist publicly. Memory math for the operator target (2x RTX 6000, 48 GB aggregate, NVLink TP2): int2-mixed-CT Qwen3.6-35B-A3B at ~14.47 GB stored fits single-card with room for KV; W4A16-class (~17.5 GB per the T4 guide) wants both cards; E=256 top-8 with N=512 intermediate means small expert GEMMs - the latency regime where Marlin's register pipeline and the split-K small-M work dominate, not the M512 throughput ceiling.

effort_value.effort_estimate: A kernel-ladder entry plus an acceptance campaign, NOT a new-kernel program: (1) wire the validated dense Turing GEMM behind MarlinExpertsBase exactly per the plan/0002 MoE contract (no separate MoE kernel architecture is planned); (2) add loud load-time gates for the two known crash classes - K/N % 128 alignment in the Marlin MoE dispatch (#38022) and the FP4-MoE binary absence below SM89 (#35922) - replacing upstream's runtime asserts; (3) run the plan/0002-style oracle + adversary + perf acceptance with expert shapes (E=256, N=512-class, top-8) in the suite, locked clocks, median-of-N. Optional parallel tracks, each cheap: humming-on-sm75 validation of the int2-mixed-CT checkpoint (backend selection + oracle diff; humming-kernels already a standard requirement) and a fused-MoE Triton config tuning sweep under the settled Triton pin (benchmark_moe.py + VLLM_TUNED_CONFIG_FOLDER). Rough size: one plan/0002-style milestone (weeks, single contributor), dominated by numerics gates rather than kernel authoring - the reuse contract is already written.
effort_value.unlocks: The operator's serving targets: the Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-class MoE checkpoints on 2x RTX 6000 over NVLink TP2 (plan/0005's operator target explicitly names 'if the target checkpoint is the MoE variant'); the int2-mixed-CT checkpoint (~14.47 GB) single-card, W4A16-class on both cards; Qwen3-30B-A3B GPTQ-Int4 (the class reference, E=128 top-8); Gemma 4 26B-A4B (E=128 top-8, Day-0 vLLM recipe); the MoE half of the Qwen3.8/Qwen3.8-Next operator focus (the dense 27B side is already covered by the dense program); and the last open dependency of plan/0005's format-interop milestone ('this checkpoint class loads, generates on both cards, and tokens/s are measured and committed').
effort_value.dependency_order: Must land first: the dense Turing GEMM performance acceptance (still open - opt2 at 23-25 TFLOP/s vs incumbent 51-57 at M512), because the MoE stage #moe-integration explicitly depends on #dense-integration and reuses the same kernel; the repack-interleave/skip_flop study that closes the dense gap is therefore also on the critical path. External prerequisites already satisfied: humming-kernels 0.1.12 (standard requirement) and PR #48918 (already in the lane tip). Can proceed in parallel: the loud-gate work (alignment/floor checks are dispatch-layer, independent of kernel perf), the acceptance-suite authoring (upstream's fused_moe/oracle/int_wna16.py harness is already in-tree as a starting point), the humming sm75 validation, and the fused-MoE Triton tuning sweep - the sweep is only meaningful after the Triton-pin decision (cross-item triton-fma-floor-sm75 / gdn-linear-attention-sm75), so sequence pin-then-tune.
effort_value.risk_notes: Numerics: INT2 group-64 experts are the risk center - the Intel model card itself warns 'measured accuracy varies significantly across different backends' and shows quantized GSM8K at 0.1585 (lmeval/vllm) vs 0.8370 (evalscope/vllm), so eval-based acceptance is unreliable and the house float64-oracle gate must run first; the card states BF16 activations while Turing+humming runs FP16 - the bf16->fp16 recast (>65504 overflow outliers) is the same contract as the GDN item; top-k weights are applied OUTSIDE the Marlin MoE kernel (routing/permute semantics are the fork's correctness responsibility, tie-breaks included). Silent fallbacks: default fused-MoE config on config-miss (warning only), humming auto-selection vs the pre-#48918 Marlin-only hard-fail, and Triton FMA codegen on modern pins - all three degrade performance or numerics without failing. Crash surface to gate loudly: K/N % 128 (#38022, gpt-oss 2880), FP4-MoE kernels missing below SM89 (#35922), and the post-#29901 T4 BF16/AWQ failure report. Upstream drift: this surface is moving fast (three humming PRs in four months plus the #53163 bugfix; scheme deprecation churn #31688/#31718) but the two known MoE bugs are closed not-planned, so nothing upstream will repair them - local gates are permanent. Accumulation-order exposure: the incumbent's FP16-accumulate Turing path (#29901) halves-precision the accumulators for throughput; the house default is FP32-accumulate (measured free on dense), but adopting the upstream FP16-accum trick would be a numerics decision to gate explicitly.
effort_value.determinism_class: Bitwise-deterministic per fixed routing for the Marlin MoE path: fixed tile traversal and k-order, no atomics in the non-split path; the split-K/global-reduce variants introduce reduction-ordering variance (the same bitwise-vs-statistical boundary as the dense item - split rows gate statistically, non-split rows exact-diff). Routing/permute and top-k selection are data-dependent but deterministic given fixed inputs; top-k TIES are the classic restart-to-restart variance source if any sort is unstable - pin the tie-break. Humming's JIT-compiled kernels have an externally-determined accumulation order: assume statistical until oracle-diffed on this hardware. The fused-MoE Triton path is deterministic per config but config selection is autotuned (time-dependent) - freeze configs in the registry row rather than autotune at serve time. Gate discipline: float64 oracle exact-diff for dequant/reference and non-split GEMM paths, median-of-N timing under locked clocks (1455 MHz protocol), and eval-harness scores never as a numerics gate (the GSM8K 0.16-vs-0.84 harness split on the int2 card is the standing counterexample).

decision.priority_signal: For doing this next: the operator focus is Qwen3.8 + Qwen3.8-Next and every fitting checkpoint in that class is MoE; the only quantized 35B-class checkpoint that fits these cards is MoE (int2-mixed-CT at ~14.5 GB); the upstream runway landed 9 days before the pin (#48918, 2026-08-19, already in the lane tip) - a rare window where the fork rides upstream sub-4-bit MoE on Turing instead of building it; plan/0005's milestone acceptance explicitly names the MoE variant; and the two crash-surface bugs are closed not-planned upstream, so the fork must build the gates regardless of when the kernel work lands. Against: the dense perf acceptance is still open and everything MoE reuses it - landing MoE on a 46-percent-of-incumbent kernel bakes in the gap; the Triton fused-MoE lane is FMA-dead under modern pins, so tuning configs buys nothing until the Triton-pin deadlock (triton-fma-floor-sm75) is settled; INT2 numerics risk is real and harness-unreliable; and the window is not closing (checkpoints and kernels are arriving, not disappearing) - sequencing after dense acceptance costs little. Net: high operator value, moderate urgency; the cheap parts (loud gates, humming sm75 validation, oracle harness) can start now without waiting on the dense kernel.
decision.recommended_probe: A gate-0 numerics probe on one card, hours not days, no timing until numerics pass: on the pinned tree, load one routed-expert block of Intel/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-int2-mixed-CT-AutoRound, force a fixed top-8 routing, and run the in-tree fused_moe int_wna16 oracle (vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/oracle/int_wna16.py) against a float64 reference - exact-diff the INT2-g64 dequant + grouped GEMM path (bitwise class), then a one-layer logits-level statistical gate vs the BF16 host run; in the same session record (a) which backend actually selects on sm75 (humming vs Marlin-only - capture the 'Using X gemm for humming moe' log line), (b) a SASS check of FFMA vs HMMA in the compiled fused-MoE Triton kernel under the current pin vs a 3.2 wheel (settles the FMA question for THIS surface), and (c) one line of load-time enforcement for K,N % 128 plus an FP4-MoE absence check in the MoE dispatch (the #38022/#35922 classes). Optional same-day extension: thread the probe through CUDA-graph capture to inherit the dense item's graph-safety evidence.
